text:
To fix the value of the constant a we must normalize the wave-function on the region where the particle is actually found (1 ≤ x ≤ 3).  
The given wave-function in that region is  

ψ(x)= a /√(1+x)  – 0.5 i .

The probability density is  

|ψ(x)|² = |a/√(1+x) – 0.5 i|²
        = (a/√(1+x))² + (0.5)²          (real² + imag²)
        = a²/(1+x) + 0.25 .

Since no particle is ever detected outside 1 ≤ x ≤ 3, the wave-function must be normalized in this interval:

∫₁³ |ψ(x)|² dx = 1 .

Compute the integral:

∫₁³ [a²/(1+x) + 0.25] dx
= a² ∫₁³ dx /(1+x)  + 0.25 ∫₁³ dx
= a² [ln(1+x)]₁³  + 0.25 (3–1)
= a² (ln4 – ln2) + 0.25(2)
= a² ln2 + 0.5 .

Set equal to 1:

a² ln2 + 0.5 = 1
⟹ a² ln2 = 0.5
⟹ a² = 0.5 / ln2
⟹ a = √(0.5 / ln2).

Numerically, ln2 ≈ 0.693147, so

a ≈ √(0.5 / 0.693147) ≈ √0.720 ≈ 0.85 .

Therefore the correct choice is (B).
